claims.text: The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi alloy is single-phase and hexagonal.
The as-deposited alloy exhibits a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited alloy has high transition hysteresis.
The as-deposited material has a low surface-to-volume ratio that limits heat exchange.
Low-energy He+ irradiation at approximately 100 K and doses of 10^13 to 10^15 ions/cm² can provide a controlled point-defect intervention.
A short anneal at 200 °C after irradiation is compatible with retaining the targeted defect regime.
The irradiation-and-annealing treatment will produce a controlled increase in point-defect density.
The induced defects will include anti-site defects and vacancy clusters distributed uniformly throughout the lattice.
Engineered point defects cause local lattice distortions.
Engineered point defects modify local magnetic exchange interactions.
Point defects broaden the distribution of local transformation energies and alter nucleation barriers.
Broadening the distribution of local transformation energies reduces the cooperativity of the first-order transition.
Reduced transition cooperativity produces a broader and more gradual magnetization change.
Irradiated samples will exhibit a broader entropy-change profile than the as-deposited baseline.
Point-defect broadening will reduce magnetic hysteresis during low-field cooling cycles.
The irradiation treatment will leave the transition temperature within ±5 K of its original value.
Transition broadening and hysteresis reduction will vary systematically with irradiation dose.
The predictions apply at fields up to approximately 2 T and only below a defect-concentration threshold at which mechanical stability begins to degrade.
